changes.comment: Add formatValueForMessage, which renders any value for a failure or diagnostic message without throwing. For every value JSON.stringify renders without throwing, the text is JSON.stringify's, cut to the length bound (200) with an ellipsis; a cut rendering is a prefix of it. It departs only where JSON.stringify would throw or produce nothing: an active-path cycle renders as "[Circular]", a BigInt as "123n", a value whose getter, Proxy trap or toJSON throws as [Unreadable], and a top-level undefined, symbol or function as a readable token. Every converter and validator failure message now uses it, so failure text changes only for inputs that previously threw and for values over the length bound. BaseConverter and GenericValidator turn a throw from the function they wrap into a Failure reading 'converter threw: <message>' or 'validator threw: <message>', so convert, validate and guard never throw (personaility#714); stack exhaustion (an InternalError, or a RangeError about the call stack) in nested converters is re-thrown to the outermost one and fails once there, while any other error is handled by the nearest boundary. stringifyLogValue no longer throws, and renders a cyclic, BigInt or partly unreadable object with formatValueForMessage instead of '[object Object]'.
